blocks.text: CON:200–222 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The final Connection block was reconsidered from first principles. The review compared five architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 73 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 17 reusable packet checks, passed 16 complete Connection-family soundness checks, and passed the complete 29-check authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: CON:2xx names communicative affordances and participant relations—endpoint participation capacity, a directed communication relation to a distinct target, and a shared co-participation relation among multiple endpoints. It does not name endpoints, channels, traffic, messages, hardware, cognition, topology, protocol, reachability, social identity, or scheduling.
CON:200 — enduring communicative participation capacity — A persistent capacity of an endpoint to participate in communicative exchange.
CON:201 — available communicative participation capacity — A communicative capacity of an endpoint that is presently available for exercise in an exchange.
CON:202 — latent communicative participation capacity — A communicative capacity of an endpoint that exists without being presently available for exercise.
CON:210 — established directed communication relation — A persistent relation that identifies a distinct endpoint as the target of communicative exchange from a reference endpoint.
CON:211 — operative directed communication relation — A directed relation from a reference endpoint to a distinct target that is presently operative as a participant link for communicative exchange.

CON:212 — unresolved directed communication relation — A directed relation from a reference endpoint to a distinct target whose status as a participant link for communicative exchange is undetermined.
CON:220 — enduring shared-participation relation — A persistent communicative relation among multiple endpoints that constitutes them as co-participants in one shared exchange context.
CON:221 — operative shared-participation relation — A communicative relation among multiple endpoints that presently operates to constitute them as co-participants in one shared exchange context.

CON:222 — potential shared-participation relation — A not-yet-realized possible communicative relation among multiple endpoints that would constitute them as co-participants in one shared exchange context.

Design boundary: an available capacity or operative relation never entails source expression, target reception, shared distribution, reachability, permission, reciprocity, compatibility, friendship, network topology, channel existence, or later realization. Lexical third-trit 2 remains distinct from runtime [2]/num and does not encode intention, plan, schedule, probability, or future time.
